tool_usage_shift.methodology: First half vs second half of all sessions by chronological order. Tokensave rule adoption was gradual (memory file + global CLAUDE.md updates over multiple sessions), so a single date pivot is misleading; the dataset-half split is the cleanest empirical cut.

rule_deltas.note: Threading rules landed; downstream parallel-work subsystems followed the pattern cleanly.
Legal-cleanup discipline. Session intensity grew separately from this rule.
Direct outcome of PRs #74+#77 retrospective. Forward-window is short; signal will mature.

pro_vs_max_estimate.methodology: Pro-period ceiling derived empirically: max single-session output in pro_period was 149,532 tokens (observed); Pro session ceiling estimated at 150,000 tokens. Any Max-period session exceeding that is counted as a session that would have been blocked or forcibly split on Pro.
pro_vs_max_estimate.estimated_savings_from_discipline_during: Without the token-efficiency + tokensave-first + visual-slice rules baked in, the same 131 Max-period sessions would have spread across roughly 222 Pro-shaped sessions — meaning ~38 sessions would have hit the Pro ceiling and forced wasted re-rolls or context-loss restarts. Per-token API price is identical across plans; the meaningful axis is session continuity, not unit cost.
pro_vs_max_estimate.disclaimer: ALL Pro-period projections are ESTIMATES. The plan-level token cap mechanic is approximate. Real-world Pro behavior may also include 5-hour rolling-window cooldowns and message-count caps not modeled here. Use these numbers as directional, not exact.

receipts.label: A.4b voxel-bake retros (PRs #74 + #77, abandoned)
receipts.story: Across 4 sessions, two PRs attempted A.4b voxel light-bake as single-PR MVP dumps. Both were abandoned after burning roughly ~3M output tokens on visual iteration that never settled. The retro produced the visual.md rule: ship ONE verifiable visual slice at a time, with a debug toggle in place from line 1, with a pause before the next slice.

receipts.label: Largest single-session output burn
receipts.story: 446-minute session producing 1,122,906 output tokens, 4,128 lines added across 27 files. Within current dataset, this is the kind of session the long-session-signals rule targets for early-cut.

receipts.label: Highest tool-error session (friction signal)
receipts.story: 17 tool errors in one session. Each error is a wasted round-trip and a small context burn. The atomic-bash-commands rule (one Bash call per logical step, no &&-chains) and the read-before-writing rule target this directly.

receipts.label: Worst-single-day token burn
receipts.story: 7 sessions in one day producing 3,923,662 output tokens combined — the day the visual-slice rule was being earned. Two of those sessions were the A.4b bake-abandonment retros.

headline_stats.most_dramatic_efficiency_gain: -18.4% change in tool-errors-per-session after modding.md landed (2026-04-25) — measured on 12 sessions before vs 131 after.

methodology_notes: Data source: per-session telemetry at ~/.claude/usage-data/session-meta/ (143 files) and ~/.claude/usage-data/facets/ (88 files).
Project names (Emberholm / Stockra) are kept because they are already in public-positioned use; no other identifying info is included.
Pro-vs-Max boundary detected as the first date where a single session output_tokens exceeded 250k — was 2026-04-25. Pre-boundary max single-session output was 149,532.

Rule-delta comparisons are 21-day before/after windows. Token-volume deltas are CONFOUNDED by project scope growth over time (M1 -> M2 work intensified) and should be read as directional. tool_errors_per_session is a cleaner signal because scope-growth raises both before AND after, cancelling the bias.
All Pro-projection numbers are ESTIMATES — annotated with "estimate": true. The Pro plan cap mechanic is approximate; treat numbers as directional.
